children: Super Micro Computer Inc. (SMCI, Financials), the server company that supplies infrastructure to AI data centers, has a demand problem most companies would love to have.
The company reported more than $60 billion of orders during its fiscal fourth quarter and guided for $65 billion to $72 billion of sales in fiscal 2027.
Shares were up about 7% Friday. But the stock still trades at almost nine times forecast non-GAAP earnings. The reason for the discount is that...

Supermicro ended fiscal 2026 with $39.1 billion in revenue, but inventory climbed to $12.9 billion as the company stocked up for rapidly growing AI deployments. This puts pressure on working capital, making cash conversion increasingly important.
Management believes client prepayments can help, and has considered being self-funded as the business grows. Another possibility is this.

Supermicro also has its Data Center Building Block Solutions that combine processing, networking, power and cooling into larger systems beyond single servers. That may alter the economics of each deployment.

The $60 billion order book indicates there is demand from investors. Next test will be if Supermicro can convert that demand into cash and improve margins. If it can, then that value discount is a lot harder to justify.

title: Super Micro Has $60B in Orders. What Comes Next?
